info.title: FoodOnTheGo API
info.description: Contract for /api/v1. Conventions: snake_case JSON; single resources are returned unwrapped; collections are {data, links, meta}; every error is {error: {code, message, details?, request_id}}; money is {amount, currency} with amount in integer minor units and an ISO 4217 currency; identifiers are public UUIDs (internal numeric ids are never exposed); timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC; countries are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; time zones are IANA ids. Every response carries X-Request-Id. Authentication: three separate bearer-token contexts (customer, restaurant, admin); a token is accepted only by routes of its own context, the account state is re-checked on every request, and sensitive endpoints are rate limited (429 rate_limited with Retry-After). tests/Feature/Foundation/OpenApiContractTest.php fails when the routes or the documented response shapes drift from this file.

The caller's cart — a guest's (X-Cart-Token) or the signed-in customer's — priced and validated against the current menu, or cart: null. A caller without session and token also receives guest_token. No route takes a cart id: a cart is only ever resolved for its owner.

post.summary: Add an item. The backend validates the item (on the active menu of that restaurant, orderable), the selection (group belongs to item, option to group, required / min / max, no duplicates, options selectable) and calculates the price. The same configuration (item + options + instructions) raises the quantity of the existing line. ONE ACTIVE CART = ONE RESTAURANT LOCATION. Errors: 404 restaurant_not_found / item_not_found; 409 cart_restaurant_conflict (details.current, details.requested), item_unavailable, option_unavailable, currency_mismatch, cart_version_conflict; 410 cart_expired; 422 invalid_customization (details.issues), quantity_limit, cart_line_limit, validation_failed.

patch.summary: Change the quantity, the selected options and / or the special instructions of a line; it is priced again by the backend. A configuration equal to another line merges the two. 404 cart_not_found / cart_line_not_found (also for a line of anybody else's cart); 409 item_unavailable / option_unavailable / restaurant_unavailable / cart_version_conflict; 410 cart_expired; 422 invalid_customization / quantity_limit.

delete.summary: Remove a line. The cart stays (possibly empty). Optional query cart_version.

post.summary: "Update my cart to the current menu": every line that can be priced today gets today's names and prices as its new baseline (PRICE_CHANGED is thereby accepted). Lines that cannot be ordered keep their issue; nothing is removed.

The confirmed restaurant switch: the current cart is closed and a cart of the other restaurant starts (with the given item, if any) in ONE transaction. If the item is not valid nothing changes. The answer carries a summary of the replaced cart. Nothing destructive ever happens without this call.

put.summary: Link the cart to one of the caller's own living journeys, on purpose ("use my current journey"). 404 journey_not_found for any other journey.

delete.summary: Remove the journey link. The cart is otherwise unchanged.

post.summary: After signing in: take over the cart built as a guest. The guest cart is named by its TOKEN (X-Cart-Token), never by an id. Policy: no account cart (or an empty / expired one) → the guest cart becomes the customer's; same restaurant → merged (same configuration adds quantities up to the item maximum, reported in claim.adjusted); different restaurants → 409 cart_merge_conflict (details.guest, details.account, details.resolutions) until `resolution` says which one to keep. The guest token is spent by the claim.

get.summary: Cart numbers for platform administrators (admin.system.view): active carts, guest carts, carts waiting for the cleanup, closed carts by outcome, and event counters of the last 24 hours. Counts only.

Pickup options for the caller's cart: ASAP, the scheduled slots, the backend's recommendation and the current selection. Calculated on the SERVER clock in the RESTAURANT's time zone from its opening hours (special hours, several periods a day, overnight), its pickup settings (preparation, lead time, buffer, interval, horizon, cut-off, capacity), the cart (preparation estimate) and — when the cart has a living journey — the traveller's estimated arrival. The restaurant is the cart's; no restaurant, customer or time can be sent. 200 also when nothing can be chosen (can_select false, issues). 404 cart_not_found; 409 cart_empty; 422 pickup_method_unavailable.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: Pickup method to answer for (default: the restaurant's first offered method)

get.summary: The pickup time chosen for the caller's cart, validated again against the cart, the restaurant and the clock — or selection: null. A selection is a choice, not a reservation.

post.summary: Choose ASAP or a scheduled slot (by its slot_key). Choosing again replaces the earlier choice: one selection per cart. The backend decides again whether the option is valid now; the choice holds no capacity (reserved is always false) and is validated again at checkout. Errors: 404 cart_not_found; 409 cart_empty, cart_invalid, cart_version_conflict, pickup_disabled, restaurant_unavailable, market_unavailable, restaurant_not_accepting, asap_unavailable (details.reason), slot_full, slot_expired; 410 cart_expired; 422 pickup_mode_unavailable, pickup_method_unavailable, slot_invalid (details.reason), slot_outside_horizon, validation_failed.

delete.summary: Forget the choice. Safe to repeat.

get.summary: What customers are offered right now with the saved pickup settings and opening hours (restaurant.profile.view): the customer pickup engine itself, run for an order that needs the default preparation time, summarised per restaurant-local day — plus warnings about a configuration that offers customers nothing. Read-only.

Pickup availability numbers for platform administrators (admin.system.view): how often availability was asked for, how often nothing could be offered, how often ASAP was possible, selections by state, and event counters of the last 24 hours. Counts only. A restaurant's pickup settings cannot be changed from the admin API.

post.summary: Open the checkout for the caller's cart. EVERYTHING is validated again — the cart, every item and option, the restaurant, its market, the pickup selection and its slot — and the total is calculated by the backend from the current menu, one promotion, the configured fee rules and the configured tax rules. 201: a new checkout (DRAFT). 200: the live checkout of this cart, when nothing changed — a second device or a repeated request gets the same one. A price that changed is never kept: the checkout shows the current total and `changes` says what moved. A checkout is not an order and charges nothing. Errors: 404 cart_not_found; 409 cart_empty, cart_invalid, item_unavailable, restaurant_unavailable, restaurant_not_accepting, market_unavailable, pickup_required, pickup_invalid, pickup_slot_full, pickup_selection_expired, cart_version_conflict, payment_in_progress — each with details.issues[] (code, message, recover); 410 cart_expired; 422 promotion_not_found, promotion_not_applicable, promotion_expired, promotion_minimum_not_met (details.minimum_spend), promotion_limit_reached, promotion_customer_limit_reached, validation_failed.

get.summary: The caller's checkout as it stands NOW. It is judged again on every read: past its expiry it is EXPIRED; when the cart, the pickup selection, a price, the promotion, a tax or fee rule, the restaurant or the required legal documents changed it is STALE (issues says why) and what it held is given back. A stale or expired checkout is replaced by opening a new one, never repaired. 404 checkout_not_found.

parameters.name: checkout

post.summary: Ask for the refund of a payment that never became an order (admin.refunds.create): a verified payment whose order cannot be made, or a second payment for a checkout already paid. Always the whole payment. Once such a refund exists the payment can no longer become an order.

Approve a refund for the amount it was asked for (admin.refunds.approve). Who asked is not who approved; with four eyes switched on the same administrator is refused (403 refund_not_authorized). Not possible while a dispute is open on the payment. Errors: 404 refund_not_found; 409 refund_invalid_transition / refund_version_conflict / refund_not_approved / refund_already_processing / refund_already_completed / refund_submission_unknown / refund_review_required / refund_failed / refund_dispute_conflict / refund_amount_exceeds_available; 422 validation_failed (any field that would set a status, an amount, a currency, a payment or a provider reference is refused); 429.

Turn a refund down, or close one that will not be made — with a reason (admin.refunds.approve). Only while nothing of it can be with the provider: a refund that was sent cannot be cancelled here. Errors: 404 refund_not_found; 409 refund_invalid_transition / refund_version_conflict / refund_not_approved / refund_already_processing / refund_already_completed / refund_submission_unknown / refund_review_required / refund_failed / refund_dispute_conflict / refund_amount_exceeds_available; 422 validation_failed (any field that would set a status, an amount, a currency, a payment or a provider reference is refused); 429.

Send an APPROVED refund to the provider (admin.refunds.issue) — the approved amount, to the method that paid. A second click finds it on its way and changes nothing. What it becomes is the provider's answer: REFUNDED, PROCESSING, FAILED — or SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN when no answer came (looked up, never sent again blindly). Errors: 404 refund_not_found; 409 refund_invalid_transition / refund_version_conflict / refund_not_approved / refund_already_processing / refund_already_completed / refund_submission_unknown / refund_review_required / refund_failed / refund_dispute_conflict / refund_amount_exceeds_available; 422 validation_failed (any field that would set a status, an amount, a currency, a payment or a provider reference is refused); 429.

Try again what can safely be tried again (admin.refunds.issue; with a reason): a refund the provider failed in a way a new attempt may fix (a NEW provider refund), or one whose submission was never answered (the provider is asked first; only when it holds nothing is the SAME request sent again). Errors: 404 refund_not_found; 409 refund_invalid_transition / refund_version_conflict / refund_not_approved / refund_already_processing / refund_already_completed / refund_submission_unknown / refund_review_required / refund_failed / refund_dispute_conflict / refund_amount_exceeds_available; 422 validation_failed (any field that would set a status, an amount, a currency, a payment or a provider reference is refused); 429.

Ask the provider again about a refund (admin.refunds.reconcile; with a reason). It changes only what the provider confirms — there is no "mark as refunded". Errors: 404 refund_not_found; 409 refund_invalid_transition / refund_version_conflict / refund_not_approved / refund_already_processing / refund_already_completed / refund_submission_unknown / refund_review_required / refund_failed / refund_dispute_conflict / refund_amount_exceeds_available; 422 validation_failed (any field that would set a status, an amount, a currency, a payment or a provider reference is refused); 429.

PickupVerifyRequest.description: Nothing about the outcome can be sent: no status, no "picked up", no customer, no override (422).

RealtimeHealth.description: Whether the realtime server (Laravel Reverb) answers. None of it changes what orders do: REST and polling do not depend on it.

RealtimeSystem.description: Counts and health only: no order of anybody, no connection of anybody.

PickupAttempt.description: One verification attempt — never the submitted secret or code

repeat_failures.description: Staff accounts with five or more failed attempts in the last 24 hours

token_state.description: Whether the device can be targeted; the token itself never appears in any answer

notifications_permission_state.description: As the app last reported it (UX context, never a security input)

current.description: True for the installation that made the call (X-Installation-Id header or the registration itself)

CustomerDevice.description: An app installation bound to the signed-in customer for push delivery (Module 33). Possession of a push token authorises nothing.

installation_id.description: A random identifier the app generates once per installation — never a hardware identifier

push_token.description: The FCM registration token (sensitive: stored encrypted, never returned, never logged)

RegisterDeviceRequest.description: The customer is the authenticated principal; a customer id is refused. Idempotent per installation.

target.description: An allow-listed screen, never a URL

reference.description: The order number for order targets

body.description: The rendered, escaped snapshot the customer saw — never a pickup secret, a code, a phone or a payment detail

CustomerNotification.description: One in-app notification (Module 33): the logical notification of a domain event for this customer. Business history stays in the order timeline; this record is bounded by retention.

NotificationDeliveryAttempt.description: One provider call — the normalised outcome, never the raw provider body or a token.

status.description: SENT = the provider accepted the message; DELIVERED only with a trustworthy receipt (no current provider gives one)

device.description: The target device of a push (summary, never the token)

retryable.description: FAILED with a live destination — the only state an administrator may send again

NotificationDelivery.description: One delivery of a notification over one channel to one destination.

customer.description: A safe reference: no phone, no e-mail

status.description: SENT = the provider accepted the message; DELIVERED only with a trustworthy receipt (no current provider gives one)

device.description: The target device of a push (summary, never the token)

retryable.description: FAILED with a live destination — the only state an administrator may send again

AdminDeliveryRow.description: One delivery of a notification over one channel to one destination.

reason.description: Audited

events.description: The domain events that produce this type

fake_push.description: Local inspection of what the development provider received (never a token) — present only with the fake driver outside production

NotificationSystem.description: Platform-wide: counts and provider health. SENT means the provider accepted the message, never that a customer read it.

TestNotificationRequest.description: Development / test environments only; audited; the customer's own devices; no free text.

NotificationProviderHealth.description: A real probe (the fcm driver mints a token; fake / log providers say so) — never green because configured.

ReviewItemFeedback.description: What the customer thought of one item of the reviewed order

average.description: SUM of the published overall ratings / their COUNT, one decimal, rounded half up; null while there is no review (never 0, never an invented number)

count.description: Number of PUBLISHED reviews of this location

ReviewRatingBrief.description: The rating of one restaurant LOCATION (Module 34). Ratings are never mixed across branches.

categories.description: Per configured category: the average of the published reviews that rated it and how many did

ReviewRatingSummary.description: Average, count and star distribution of a location's PUBLISHED reviews. Hidden, rejected, removed and waiting reviews are not counted.

ReviewPublicResponse.description: The restaurant's published answer; never the staff member's name

images.description: Always false: review photos are not implemented

policy_status.description: The windows and limits are development defaults pending business approval

ReviewConfig.description: The review policy a client needs to draw the form (config/reviews.php)

reason.description: ELIGIBLE or why not; another customer's order is 404, never a reason

can_edit.description: Whether the existing review may still be changed

category_ratings.description: Optional category ratings: configured category code → whole stars

comment.description: Plain text in any language; rendered as text by every client

verified_order.description: Always true: a review exists only for a completed order of its author. Derived; never an input.

version.description: Send it back to change the review

CustomerReview.description: The customer's own review of one completed order (Module 34)

created.description: false when this call repeated a submission that already exists (a retry)

OrderReviewState.description: Whether the order can be reviewed now, the review if there is one, and the policy

client_submission_id.description: A token of the client for this submission: the same token again answers the same review

SubmitReviewRequest.description: Ratings, tags, item feedback and text ONLY. The customer, the restaurant, the status and "verified" are decided by the server from the order: any other field is refused (422).

version.description: The version the client loaded (409 version_conflict when it is not the current one)

UpdateReviewRequest.description: Only the fields that are sent change

ReportReviewRequest.description: A report asks an administrator to look; it changes nothing by itself

display_name.description: First name and the initial of the last one — the only thing of the customer that is public

category_ratings.description: Optional category ratings: configured category code → whole stars

comment.description: Plain text in any language; rendered as text by every client

PublicReview.description: A PUBLISHED review as anybody may read it. No phone, e-mail, account id, order number, journey, payment or pickup detail.

category_ratings.description: Optional category ratings: configured category code → whole stars

comment.description: Plain text in any language; rendered as text by every client

reported.description: Whether the caller already reported this review

RestaurantReview.description: A published review of one of the caller's locations. The restaurant can answer and report; it can never change or remove it.

ReviewResponseRequest.description: The first call publishes the one official response; a later call edits it (the previous text is kept)

review.description: In the case list: the review the case is about (id, status, rating, text, restaurant, order number, version)

ReviewModerationCase.description: One open question about one review: flagged by the automated screening (plain rules, not AI) or reported

category_ratings.description: Optional category ratings: configured category code → whole stars

comment.description: Plain text in any language; rendered as text by every client

AdminReview.description: A review as a moderator sees it; the detail adds the cases, the previous versions and the audit trail

counts.description: Reviews per status within the caller's market scope, plus `all` and `reported` (an open case)

reason.description: Required to hide, reject or restore (3–300 characters); recorded and audited

ModerateReviewRequest.description: A decision against the state the review is in: 409 review_state_conflict when another administrator already decided

ResolveReviewCaseRequest.description: Closes a case without touching the review

state.description: What the customer may do about a review of this order

OrderReviewBlock.description: Module 34: "Write review" only when ELIGIBLE; "View your review" when REVIEWED

reference.description: A short reference to read to support. It opens nothing.

status.description: REQUIRED = owed and not with the payment provider yet (also when it is approved); PROCESSING = with the payment provider, NOT confirmed; REFUNDED = confirmed by the provider; UNDER_REVIEW = FoodOnTheGo is looking at it (the customer does nothing and is not charged again)

label.description: Neutral words for the customer; never an internal note

CustomerRefund.description: One refund of the customer's own order. No provider reference, no approval detail, no failure reason. A request nobody approved and a cancelled one are not listed.

status.description: The order's derived refund status in the CUSTOMER's words (Module 35): REQUIRED = a refund is due and has not been sent to the provider yet; PROCESSING = with the provider, not confirmed; PARTIALLY_REFUNDED / REFUNDED = confirmed by the provider; UNDER_REVIEW = FoodOnTheGo is looking at it (the internal states FAILED and REVIEW_REQUIRED are never sent to a customer). The order's own status and its payment state are never changed by a refund.

refunded.description: Confirmed by the payment provider — nothing else counts as refunded

pending.description: Owed or on its way, not confirmed yet

timing_note.description: Always null: no number of days is promised — when a refund shows on a statement depends on the customer's bank

CustomerOrderRefunds.description: The refunds of a paid order as the refund domain has them. Null for an order that was never paid for (nothing can be refunded).

financial_effect.description: What cancelling does to the money — decided by the configured policy, never by the client. Null when the order cannot be cancelled.

refundable_amount.description: For FULL_REFUND: what is left of the payment at this moment

OrderCancellationQuote.description: What cancelling this order would mean, as the server decides it. Shown to the customer before they confirm.

expected_version.description: The order version the client saw (409 order_version_conflict when the order moved meanwhile)

CustomerCancelOrderRequest.description: A reason ONLY. No refund amount, currency, financial effect or status can be sent: the policy decides what happens to the money.

status.description: DERIVED from the order's refunds (Module 35): REQUIRED = a refund is owed and the provider does not have it yet (not approved, approved, or about to be sent); PROCESSING = with the provider (or possibly with it: an unanswered submission), not confirmed; PARTIALLY_REFUNDED / REFUNDED = confirmed by the provider for a part / all of what was paid; FAILED / REVIEW_REQUIRED = a person at FoodOnTheGo is looking at it. The order's own status and its payment state are never changed by a refund.

amount.description: Owed, on its way or refunded for this order

controls.description: A restaurant has no refund controls: rejecting a paid order starts the refund workflow by itself

RestaurantOrderRefund.description: Whether money is going back for an order. No refund ids, no provider. Null for an order that was never paid for.

in_flight.description: Held by refunds that are asked for, approved, on their way or not understood yet

available.description: paid − refunded − in_flight − charged_back: the most a new refund may ask for. Recalculated on the server at every action.

RefundBalance.description: What one payment can still give back. The database refuses in_flight + refunded > paid.

customer.description: A reference only: the refund screens are not a customer directory

AdminRefund.description: A refund in the administrators' list (Module 35)

refund_status.description: DERIVED from the order's refunds (Module 35): REQUIRED = a refund is owed and the provider does not have it yet (not approved, approved, or about to be sent); PROCESSING = with the provider (or possibly with it: an unanswered submission), not confirmed; PARTIALLY_REFUNDED / REFUNDED = confirmed by the provider for a part / all of what was paid; FAILED / REVIEW_REQUIRED = a person at FoodOnTheGo is looking at it. The order's own status and its payment state are never changed by a refund.

status.description: Stays VERIFIED after a refund

customer.description: A reference only: the refund screens are not a customer directory

approval.description: Who approved it — never the same field as who asked

message.description: FoodOnTheGo's own sentence — never the provider's

status.description: The provider's own status word

receipt.description: Our reference of the provider refund = its idempotency key

provider_detail.description: References and states only. No key, no secret, no payload.

attempts.description: Every question asked of the provider, with what came back

mark_refunded.description: There is no way to mark a refund as refunded

actions.description: What the refund's state allows AND the caller's permissions allow

RefundQueues.description: How many refunds wait in each operational queue, for the markets the caller may see

type.description: FULL = everything that is left of the payment (the server works it out); PARTIAL = amount_minor

amount_minor.description: PARTIAL only: a whole number of minor units > 0 and not more than what is left. A REQUEST — checked on the server against the payment's balance at this moment.

currency.description: Optional; when sent it has to be the payment's currency (422 refund_currency_mismatch)

AdminRefundRequestForOrder.description: No status, approved amount, payment, customer or provider reference can be sent.

AdminRefundRequestForPayment.description: Always the whole payment; the reason is read from the payment (PAYMENT_ORDER_FAILURE or DUPLICATE_PAYMENT). No amount, currency, type or reason can be sent.

reason.description: Required for reject, retry and reconcile; written to the audit log

AdminRefundDecisionRequest.description: Nothing about a refund can be set by hand: a status, an amount, a currency or a reference in this request is refused.

health.description: The provider's refund operations, counted apart from its payment operations

amounts_minor.description: Minor units per currency and state. Operational totals — NOT settlement or accounting figures.

RefundMetrics.description: Counts and states of the refund domain. Numbers only.

amount_deducted.description: What the provider took back (non-zero once a dispute is lost)

actions.description: Read-only: a dispute is answered with the provider, not here

AdminDispute.description: A dispute / chargeback a provider reported on a payment (Module 35 foundation). Written only from verified provider events. A dispute is NOT a refund.

scenario.description: PROCESSED / FAILED: the bank finishes the refund the fake provider holds. NEXT_*: what the fake provider answers to the next refund request.

dispute_reference.description: Required for every scenario but OPEN
